framework.name: expo
framework.notes: React Native mobile app (react-native 0.85.3, react 19.2.3), NOT a web React SPA — no vite/next anywhere. expo-router ~56.2.11 supplies both screens and server endpoints (files ending in +api.ts). app.json sets web.output='server' and web.bundler='metro', so the same routes can be exported for web, but the product targets iOS/Android via expo-dev-client + native prebuild. AGENTS.md pins the correct docs to https://docs.expo.dev/versions/v56.0.0/.

monorepo.notes: Single Expo app at repo root (no workspaces field). legal/ is a second, independent deployable inside the same repo: a static-assets Cloudflare Worker (legal/wrangler.jsonc) serving landing/privacy/terms/support HTML.

auth.notes: Google + Apple OAuth only (src/hooks/useSSOAuth.ts strategies 'oauth_google' | 'oauth_apple'; src/app/(auth)/sign-in.tsx has exactly two buttons). No email-password or magic-link UI exists. Client gating is a Redirect to /sign-in in src/app/(home)/_layout.tsx; every API route re-verifies 'Authorization: Bearer <Clerk session token>' server-side in src/lib/auth.ts via verifyToken. No role/admin concept anywhere in the tree.

routes.notes: 8 screens + 8 API route files (plus 3 _layout.tsx navigators not counted). Paths taken from the git tree of src/app/; expo-router maps (home)/index.tsx to '/' and [id].tsx to a dynamic segment. Only /sign-in is public. '/api/inngest' is Inngest's serve endpoint and '/api/webhooks/clerk' is the Svix-verified Clerk webhook.

env.notes: All values empty in .env.example — no secrets committed. The 11 uncommented .env.example names are required for dev; INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY / INNGEST_EVENT_KEY are present but commented out ('only needed in production'); SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN appears only in README's env list, not in .env.example. SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN is needed for the Sentry Expo plugin's source-map upload; the EXPO_PUBLIC_ prefix is inlined at build time per the comment in src/lib/env.ts. Runtime is hard-failing: src/db/index.ts throws at module import when DATABASE_URL is missing and src/lib/env.ts getters throw on every other secret, so any /api route import fails before serving a request.

deploy.notes: No Dockerfile, no docker-compose, no eas.json, no CI. README's run instructions are 'npm install' then 'npx expo run:ios' / 'npx expo run:android' — a native prebuild toolchain (Xcode / Android Studio) is required because of expo-dev-client and the config plugins; there is no web-only or container path. No build script exists in package.json. DB schema is applied with drizzle-kit push (src/drizzle.config.ts sets out './drizzle' but no drizzle/ directory is committed, so there are zero migration files). paas_coupling is only the bundled marketing/legal site: legal/ is a Cloudflare static-assets Worker (name 'triply-legal') deployed independently of the app.

tests.notes: Zero test files at any depth (tree grep for test/spec/__tests__/vitest/jest/playwright returns nothing) and no .github directory at all — gh api repos/.../contents/.github returns 404, so the repo has no CI, no issue templates, no CodeRabbit config despite the README advertising 'AI Code Review with CodeRabbit'. The only JSON under .claude/skills/*/evals/ are Claude Code skill evaluation specs, not application tests.

vendor.name: clerk
vendor.what_it_does: user auth/sessions (Google + Apple SSO), session-token verification on every API route, and user.created/updated/deleted webhooks that drive DB sync
vendor.swap_target_hint: better-auth (mobile OAuth needs a device flow; expect custom work)

vendor.name: neon
vendor.what_it_does: hosted serverless Postgres reached over HTTP with @neondatabase/serverless + drizzle-orm/neon-http
vendor.swap_target_hint: supabase / any Postgres (swap the neon-http driver for node-postgres)

vendor.name: openai
vendor.what_it_does: trip itinerary + budget generation and the chat assistant; Structured Outputs via zodResponseFormat on gpt-4o-mini (90%) / gpt-4o (10%)
vendor.swap_target_hint: any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Anthropic/Groq/local) behind the same zod schemas

vendor.name: inngest
vendor.what_it_does: durable background jobs: trip-generation pipeline with step.run, a weighted model experiment, and the Clerk user-sync functions
vendor.swap_target_hint: self-hosted Inngest or a queue + worker (BullMQ/Trigger.dev)

vendor.name: imagekit
vendor.what_it_does: re-hosts Unsplash covers and stores user-uploaded trip cover images; delivery-time transform URLs (ik.imagekit.io)

vendor.name: unsplash
vendor.what_it_does: destination cover photos via api.unsplash.com/search/photos, with required photographer attribution stored on the trips row
vendor.swap_target_hint: Pexels / Picsum / own asset library (attribution fields must be kept for ToS compliance)

vendor.name: sentry
vendor.what_it_does: crash/error tracking plus manual gen_ai spans and structured logs; mobile replay; app.json hardcodes org 'codesistency-gs' / project 'triply-tutorial'
vendor.swap_target_hint: remove or point at your own Sentry org (no vendor lock beyond DSN)

pitfalls.detail: src/db/index.ts throws 'Missing DATABASE_URL' at module import and src/lib/env.ts getters throw for CLERK_SECRET_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY / UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY / the three IMAGEKIT_* vars, so importing any /api route (or running Inngest functions) without a complete .env fails immediately. There is no .env in the repo and no offline/mock mode.
package.json declares "reset-project": "node ./scripts/reset-project.js" but no scripts/ directory exists anywhere in the tree, so `npm run reset-project` fails with MODULE_NOT_FOUND.
pitfalls.evidence: package.json scripts vs gh api git/trees/master?recursive=1 (no scripts/ path)

pitfalls.detail: drizzle.config.ts sets out: './drizzle' but no drizzle/ directory is committed — there are zero migration files; schema changes are applied only with `npm run db:push` (drizzle-kit push) against a live Neon database. Anyone expecting migrate/rollback files finds none.
pitfalls.evidence: drizzle.config.ts + git tree (no drizzle/ path), package.json scripts

pitfalls.detail: Native-only build: expo-dev-client, @expo/ui, expo-glass-effect, expo-symbols, react-native-maps 1.27.2, react-native-reanimated 4.3.1 + react-native-worklets. It cannot run in Expo Go or as a plain web app — `npx expo run:ios|android` (Xcode/Android Studio) or a fresh EAS setup is required.
pitfalls.evidence: package.json dependencies, app.json plugins, README run instructions, AGENTS.md

pitfalls.detail: src/inngest/client.ts hardcodes `isDev: true`, so Inngest signature validation is skipped and events are assumed to go to a local dev server; production wiring (INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY/INNGEST_EVENT_KEY, which are commented out in .env.example) needs a code change, and the documented dev flow requires `npm run inngest` (inngest-cli) running alongside the app.

README's env list and .env.example disagree: README omits INNGEST_DEV and lists SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN that .env.example does not contain; the README also claims CodeRabbit AI review and 'App Store-Ready' structure while the repo has no .github directory and no store config. Follow the code, not the README.
pitfalls.evidence: README.md vs .env.example vs gh api repos/.../contents/.github (404)

pitfalls.detail: Expo SDK 56 with React Native 0.85 / React 19.2 and a caret-free pin set (react 19.2.3, react-native-maps 1.27.2, reanimated 4.3.1). The navigation uses expo-router's 'unstable' native-tabs API (expo-router/unstable-native-tabs) and AGENTS.md forbids switching to a JS tab bar, so upgrades are risky and iOS-Liquid-Glass behaviour is platform-specific.

AGENTS.md ends with stray literal '</content>' / '</invoke>' tag lines (file is 1776 bytes and those tags are really in it) — a pasted AI-transcript artifact, harmless but confusing to an agent that parses the file. AGENTS.md also forbids ever starting the dev server, which conflicts with a fresh checkout where nothing is running.
pitfalls.evidence: AGENTS.md (tail bytes verified via curl | od -c)

pitfalls.detail: Repo carries ~29 MB of committed binaries: design/ mockup PNGs (~15 MB) plus assets/images (auth-bg.png 2.2 MB, world.png 1.1 MB, screenshot-for-readme.png 1.4 MB); legal/ui-inspiration.png is 5.8 MB and excluded from the Worker only via legal/.assetsignore. Sparse/shallow clones save real time.

verdict.best_for: A tutorial-grade but genuinely complete Expo/React Native reference for an AI trip-planner or similar AI-generation mobile product — real auth, real Postgres schema, a durable Inngest generation pipeline, streaming chat assistant and image pipeline — best used as a working starting point to rebuild the same feature set rather than as maintained infrastructure.
verdict.weak_for: Anything expecting production maturity: it is a 6-day, single-author, 16-commit tutorial build with no tests, no CI, no Docker/migrations, hardcoded dev-mode Inngest, client-side-only route gating, no admin/roles, no i18n, no payments and no email — and it cannot run in Expo Go or a container, so a native toolchain (or a new EAS setup) is a prerequisite for even the first screen.
verdict.swap_burden: medium — Clerk, Neon, Inngest, ImageKit, Unsplash and Sentry are all isolated behind thin single-purpose modules (src/lib/auth.ts, src/db/index.ts + drizzle, src/inngest/*, src/lib/images.ts, src/lib/env.ts), so each swap is small, but the mobile-only toolchain, hardcoded isDev Inngest and client-side route protection must be fixed before anything is deployable.

Runtime behaviour — per the remote-only rule nothing was installed or executed, so 'npm install' success, native prebuild/EAS build outcome, and the actual drizzle-kit push result are unverified. Dependency resolution was spot-checked only: all 8 sampled packages (@neondatabase/serverless 1.1.0, imagekit 6.0.0, inngest 4.21.0, svix 2.5.0, nativewind 4.2.7, typescript 7.0.2, expo 57.0.24, react-native-maps 1.29.8) return HTTP 200 from registry.npmjs.org — no phantom dependency found, but the full 42-declaration set and the ~756 KB package-lock.json were not exhaustively re-resolved.
Exact LOC — estimated from tracked blob byte sizes divided by 35; no line counts were read file-by-file (would need a clone).
Vercel/metrics for the landing page, real store-readiness, and whether the referenced Clerk/Sentry/ImageKit/Neon accounts still exist — not measurable from the repo.
Component count is 1 by directory (src/components/AuthIcons.tsx); screen-local UI blocks inside src/app/** were not counted individually, so 1 understates real UI-surface count.

Two of the three deepest screens (src/app/trip/[id].tsx 21.9 KB, src/app/generate-trip.tsx 17.4 KB) were skimmed for imports/route shape only, not read in full — an unlisted feature or hardcoded block could hide there.

I did not audit .claude/skills/** (37 KB of vendored Clerk Claude Code skill markdown) or skills-lock.json hashes beyond confirming there is no executable/hook content in .claude/settings.json (which contains only {"enabledPlugins": {"expo@claude-plugins-official": true}}).
